## Solution

**Setup.** Place the white king at corner **a1** (all corners are equivalent by symmetry). We place one black bishop and one white bishop on the remaining 63 squares (no two pieces on the same square). The condition "neither checks the king of the opposite color" means:

- **Black bishop** must not check the **white king** (the king of opposite color to black).
- **White bishop** has no opposite-color king on the board (no black king exists), so it faces **no constraint**.

**Key geometric fact.** The only diagonal through a1 containing other squares is the long diagonal a1–h8 (since a1 is a corner, the other diagonal direction is empty). Thus a black bishop checks the white king at a1 if and only if it sits on one of **b2, c3, d4, e5, f6, g7, h8** (7 squares) **and** no piece blocks the path between it and a1.

Label these diagonal squares as positions 1 through 7 (b2=1, c3=2, …, h8=7), with the king at position 0.

---

**Counting valid configurations.**

**Case 1: Black bishop is NOT on the a1–h8 diagonal.**

The black bishop can occupy any of 63 − 7 = **56** squares. The white bishop (unconstrained) can then occupy any of the remaining **62** squares.

$$\text{Subtotal} = 56 \times 62 = 3472.$$

**Case 2: Black bishop IS on the diagonal, at position $i$ ($1 \le i \le 7$), but is blocked.**

The black bishop checks the king unless the white bishop sits **between** the king (position 0) and the black bishop (position $i$), i.e., on one of positions $1, 2, \ldots, i-1$. There are $i - 1$ such blocking squares.

For each $i$, the number of valid (black bishop, white bishop) pairs is $i - 1$.

$$\text{Subtotal} = \sum_{i=1}^{7}(i-1) = 0 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 21.$$

(When the white bishop blocks, the black bishop does not check the white king, and the white bishop has no opposite-color king to check — so the configuration is valid.)

---

**Verification via complementary counting.**

Total unrestricted placements: $63 \times 62 = 3906$.

Invalid placements (black bishop checks king): black bishop at position $i$, white bishop NOT in a blocking position. For each $i$, the white bishop has $62 - (i-1) = 63 - i$ non-blocking choices.

$$\text{Invalid} = \sum_{i=1}^{7}(63 - i) = 62 + 61 + 60 + 59 + 58 + 57 + 56 = 413.$$

$$\text{Valid} = 3906 - 413 = 3493. \checkmark$$

---

**Total valid configurations:**

$$3472 + 21 = \boxed{3493}.$$

### PROOF COMPLETE

**Setup.** Place the white king at corner **a1** (all corners are equivalent by symmetry). We place one black bishop and one white bishop on the remaining 63 squares (no two pieces on the same square). The condition "neither checks the king of the opposite color" means:

- **Black bishop** must not check the **white king** (the king of opposite color to black).
- **White bishop** has no opposite-color king on the board (no black king exists), so it faces **no constraint**.

**Key geometric fact.** The only diagonal through a1 containing other squares is the long diagonal a1–h8 (since a1 is a corner, the other diagonal direction is empty). Thus a black bishop checks the white king at a1 if and only if it sits on one of **b2, c3, d4, e5, f6, g7, h8** (7 squares) **and** no piece blocks the path between it and a1.

Label these diagonal squares as positions 1 through 7 (b2=1, c3=2, …, h8=7), with the king at position 0.

---

**Counting valid configurations.**

**Case 1: Black bishop is NOT on the a1–h8 diagonal.**

The black bishop can occupy any of 63 − 7 = **56** squares. The white bishop (unconstrained) can then occupy any of the remaining **62** squares.
